newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels reject statement on Mobutu stepping down.
newsitem.headline: Rebels reject statement on Mobutu stepping down.

text.p: Zairean rebels on Friday dismissed a Kinshasa statement that President Mobutu Sese Seko would step aside, leaving the government in charge.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila's foreign affairs spokesman Karaha Bizima told reporters:"The (rebel) executive committee decided that we reject categorically those declarations by those irresponsible people in Kinshasa who do not want anything else but to see bloodshed in the capital."
Government spokesman Kin-Kiey Mulumba read the Kinshasa statement after Mobutu left for his northern jungle palace at Gbadolite, triggering intense speculation that he was going into exile.
Bizima said:"We ask our population in all the country specifically in Kinshasa to stay in their houses, be calm and not to do anything to jeopardise the situation in Kinshasa.

"We ask the military, the remains of the military of Mobutu, not to fight any more, not to loot, not to do anything unlawful and to await the announcement which will be made tomorrow by President Kabila."

Of the cabinet statement on Mobutu stepping down he said:"The power would remain in the hands of the government and the parliament, according to their constitution, which does not actually exist in this country."
